transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-22
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: 38 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Sam (Redwood SE), Alex (Zephyr CTO), Maya (Zephyr SRE), Rohit (Head of Search), Lee (PM)

Summary:
Quick hosted API demo showing embeddings + reranking workflow for search relevance. Walkthrough of Redwood Console for monitoring, and Optimize recommendations (batching / quantization hints). Customer asked about latency, vector DB integrations, security (SOC2/KMS), and pilot scoping. Agreed to share pricing, security docs, and run 1-week pilot.

Topics covered:
- Hosted embeddings endpoint and dimensionality/options
- Reranking endpoint (generate scores vs re-rank tokens)
- Integration with vector DBs and hybrid search stacks
- Console observability and Optimize recommendations
- Security and compliance (SOC2, SSO, KMS, VPC)

Action items (quick list repeated): Jordan to send pricing and pilot doc; Priya to share eval harness and sample prompts; Maya to surface dataset sample.

Transcript body:
[00:00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan Miller from Redwood - I'm the AE on this account. With me today is Priya Nair, our SE, and Sam who will help run the demo. How's everyone doing at Zephyr?
[00:00:12] Alex: Good thanks, Jordan. Busy week but excited to see what you have.
[00:00:15] Maya: Morning, yes thanks. We want to focus on search relevance, embeddings pipeline, and where reranking fits in.
[00:00:22] Jordan: Great. Quick agenda: we'll show the hosted embeddings endpoint, then the rerank API, walk through a Console view for latency/cost, and finish with Optimize suggestions for throughput. We'll leave time for Q&A and pilot next steps.
[00:00:35] Priya: I'll start with a high-level — the hosted flow is lightweight: you call /v1/embeddings with your text, get vectors back, store them in your vector DB of choice, then for search we support two approaches: 1) similarity + client-side rerank using our rerank endpoint which returns scores and tokens, or 2) server-side rerank where we handle candidate generation and reranking for you.
[00:01:00] Rohit: Sorry, quick clarification — when you say rerank endpoint, is that scoring only? Are you returning token-level deltas or the full ranked doc?
[00:01:08] Priya: Good question. We offer a couple of modes. The simplest is score-only: you POST the query + candidate doc texts and we return a score per candidate. There's also a detailed mode that returns highlighted spans and a small explanation string. Both can be tuned. Note that score-only is lower latency and lower cost.
[00:01:28] Lee: What's the typical latency we should expect for score-only with hosted? Sub-100ms?
[00:01:33] Priya: For most 1–5 candidate reranks, we generally see 50–120ms median depending on model and sequence length. If you push 50 candidates, it goes up; we have batching optimizations but there's a tradeoff with tail latency.
[00:01:48] Maya: Our P50 target is 150ms for inline search — can you hit that?
[00:01:52] Sam: Usually yes on hosted with smaller models and a tight prompt; for higher-accuracy models you might be around 120–250ms. The Console lets you pin a model variant or enable a fast fallback. Also Optimize will recommend batching/cache tweaks.
[00:02:07] Alex: Are you compatible with our vector DB? We're on Elastic + an in-house vector layer for older docs.
[00:02:12] Priya: Absolutely. Customers combine Elastic for metadata filtering and Redwood embeddings stored in any vector DB — Pinecone, Weaviate, Milvus, or your in-house. We return normalized vectors; we also include metadata and IDs so your hybrid ranking works.
[00:02:27] Rohit: Do you provide embeddings dims / model choices out of the box? We rely on 1536 dim for backward compatibility.
[00:02:33] Priya: We have multiple models: 512, 768, 1536, and 2048 dims depending on the model family. If you need 1536 we can default to that. We also expose quantized variants for cost reduction.
[00:02:44] Rohit: Good. Also, can you do incremental KV cache or session affinity for rerank state? We have multi-turn queries.
[00:02:51] Priya: For reranker state we don't keep user session state in hosted — it's stateless per request — but for generation paths we optimize KV cache internally. For multi-turn workflows we recommend sending relevant context slices; Optimize can advise on prefix caching to reduce tokens and cost.
[00:03:08] Alex: Security — we need SOC2, SSO, and KMS. Any blockers there for hosted?
[00:03:14] Jordan: We're SOC2 compliant and can provide the report. For SSO we support SAML/SSO and RBAC in the Console. For key management, hosted supports customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations — we'll share the KMS integration guide after the call.
[00:03:30] Maya: And data residency? Some of our EU users' data must not leave region.
[00:03:34] Jordan: We have region-specific endpoints. For strict residency you can also choose Dedicated or Private deployments, but many customers meet residency needs with hosted regional endpoints and data controls. We'll flag that in the security pack.
[00:03:46] Lee: Can you show the Console quick? I'd like to see monitoring for token costs per route.
[00:03:51] Sam: Sure, switching over — I'm going to share my screen. (screen share noises) Here's the Console dashboard, per-route latency, per-token cost breakdown, and trace view. You can see we have rollout controls if you want to A/B a reranker variant.
[00:04:10] Priya: One cool bit is the Optimize tab. It scans your traffic shape and recommends batching thresholds, quantization levels, and cache TTL for prefixes. For a typical search workload where queries are short and candidates are small, Optimize often recommends small batch windows to keep latency low while still achieving batching benefit.
[00:04:28] Rohit: Is that automated or advisory? Can we auto-apply?
[00:04:31] Sam: Right now it's advisory but you can export the recommended config. Some enterprise customers enable auto-apply via our API with guardrails.
[00:04:39] Alex: How do we measure relevance improvements? We already have a labeled set.
[00:04:44] Priya: We can run an eval harness against your labeled set. We'll run baseline embeddings similarity ranking vs embeddings + rerank and show MAP/NDCG/Precision@k improvements. Priya: In past customers we've seen up to 8–18% NDCG uplift on hard queries when adding a reranker.
[00:05:00] Maya: That sounds promising. If we do a pilot, what data do you need?
[00:05:04] Priya: Ideally: 1) sample of queries and labeled relevance, 2) a few thousand candidate docs or embeddings export, and 3) your current vector DB query flow. From there we can provision a hosted PoC project and run end-to-end tests.
[00:05:18] Alex: Can Redwood host the index for the pilot or do we need to give you DB access?
[00:05:22] Jordan: For hosted PoCs we usually ask for a sanitized data export. We don't take raw PII if customers are uncomfortable; you can run the eval harness locally and we can accept embeddings and anonymized IDs.
[00:05:34] Lee: Pricing — ballpark per-100k queries?
[00:05:37] Jordan: I'll send a full pricing sheet after the call. Ballpark depends on model and rerank candidates; for a typical embeddings+rerank stack we model token-based embeddings costs plus reranker per-call cost. We'll include example unit economics for 1M / 10M queries.
[00:05:49] Rohit: Any limits on candidate count? We often score 20–50 candidates at rerank.
[00:05:54] Priya: We support that. Score-only is more cost-effective. For large candidate sets we recommend two-stage: light similarity prune to top 50 then rerank top 10 in score-only mode. That hits good latency/cost balance.
[00:06:10] Alex: Can we do on-the-fly hybrid search — you do the filtering and ranking server-side?
[00:06:15] Priya: We have a server-side hybrid option where Redwood receives the query and filters via metadata, retrieves candidates, and returns final ranks. That requires a little more integration but is available for Dedicated/Pvt customers; hosted can do it for pilots with some caveats.
[00:06:29] Maya: We have strict audit requirements. Are audit logs available for each request?
[00:06:33] Jordan: Yes, request-level logs and trace IDs. We can configure longer retention if needed as an add-on.
[00:06:40] (brief crosstalk)
[00:06:45] Priya: Ok demo time. I'll run an embeddings call first and show the vector output, then a rerank scoring example.
[00:06:52] (typing)
[00:06:58] Priya: Posting example now — here is a call to /v1/embeddings with a sample query: returns a 1536-d vector for the sample doc, plus normalized magnitude. Note: the transcription on the console sometimes abbreviates the vector output for readability.
[00:07:12] Rohit: The vector looks normalized — what's the float precision? 32-bit? 16-bit?
[00:07:16] Priya: Default is float32; we have quantized outputs (int8, fp16) for some models. The Console flags when a vector is quantized.
[00:07:25] Lee: Next the rerank call?
[00:07:27] Priya: Yes — here's a POST to /v1/rerank with query text and 10 candidate blobs. Score-only mode returns a score array. I'm going to run both score-only and the explain mode to show the difference.
[00:07:41] (demo results)
[00:07:44] Priya: Score-only returned median 82ms on this sample. Explain mode returned 170ms and included a 1–2 line rationale per doc. The console shows cost per call estimate.
[00:07:58] Maya: Those numbers look usable. In our production shards we worry about 99th percentile. Do you have tail lat guidance?
[00:08:05] Sam: Tail depends on model size, I/O, and if you're using a server-side candidate generation. We instrument per-request traces and you can set SLO-based fallback to a smaller model or cached response.
[00:08:18] Alex: Any caveats with rate limits? We'll be doing bursts during traffic spikes.
[00:08:22] Jordan: We support rate limits and burst policies. For bursty workloads we recommend a reserved capacity commit (Dedicated) or a burst pool on Hosted which we can configure.
[00:08:33] Rohit: How hard is the migration from our current pipeline? We have a node service that does search + a custom scoring layer.
[00:08:39] Priya: It should be straightforward — embeddings endpoint is a REST call, you store vectors in your DB. For rerank, we accept plain text blobs or precomputed embeddings as input. We have SDKs (Node, Python) and code examples. We'll share a quickstart repo.
[00:08:55] Lee: Will you share a sample integration with Elastic?
[00:08:58] Priya: Yes, we'll include an integration snippet: query Elastic for metadata filters + top-k vector candidates, then call Redwood rerank for final ordering. There's also a sample KNN pipeline with Elastic's vector plugin in our docs.
[00:09:09] Alex: On observability — will the Console show token-level costs by API key? We need to allocate costs to teams.
[00:09:15] Sam: Yes, Console has per-token cost breakdown and route-level and API-key level reports. You can also export CSV for chargeback.
[00:09:24] Maya: One more: encryption at rest — do you support CMEK?
[00:09:28] Jordan: Yes, Customer-Managed Encryption Keys supported for hosted on certain plans; we'll share the KMS integration note.
[00:09:36] (short pause)
[00:09:42] Jordan: Alright, demo complete. Any other questions?
[00:09:46] Rohit: A few noted earlier: pilot data and timeline. We're thinking 1-week pilot to validate NDCG uplift and latency. What's the minimum scope?
[00:09:55] Priya: Minimum: ~5k labeled query-doc pairs or a few thousand queries plus candidate sets; we'll run baseline vs rerank and produce an eval report. We can also run live A/B traffic if you want.
[00:10:08] Alex: Sounds good. We'll try to get the sample by end of week.
[00:10:12] Maya: Also include cost projection for 10M queries since that's our growth target.
[00:10:16] Jordan: Will do — I'll attach a modeled spreadsheet.
[00:10:20] Lee: Any mention of competitor differences here? We looked at Pinecone for vector store but they don't do reranking like this out of the box, right?
[00:10:28] Priya: Correct — Pinecone is great for vector storage and similarity; Redwood adds the rerank layer and the inference runtime and observability. Elastic can do vectors too but you'll need more engineering for model-based rerank.
[00:10:38] Rohit: Would you expect to see cost savings using quantized models vs full fp32?
[00:10:42] Sam: Yes quantized models and batching can reduce per-token cost substantially — sometimes 2–3x. Optimize will recommend quantization where it doesn't harm quality based on your eval set.
[00:10:54] Alex: Great. Let's capture next steps.
[00:10:58] Jordan: Recap: Jordan will send pricing and contract starter + modeled spreadsheet; Priya will share evaluation harness and sample prompts; we schedule a technical deep dive next week to kick off the pilot. Any objections?
[00:11:12] Alex: No objections.
[00:11:14] Maya: Good. Thanks everyone.
[00:11:17] Jordan: Thanks all — we'll follow up via email with links: pricing PDF, SOC2 pack, KMS guide, and the quickstart repo.
[00:11:25] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcript quality: occasional stitch errors around code snippets, some proper nouns misrecognized (Zephyr sometimes shows as "Zephir" in the raw auto-transcript). References shared: demo deck (link: https://app.redwood.ai/decks/hosted-embeddings-rerank-demo), security-pack (link: https://redwood.ai/security/soc2.zip), sample benchmark spreadsheet (link: https://redwood.ai/pilots/zephyr-benchmark.xlsx).
